claims.text: The governing distance measurement is the trace, not the receipt, and on it this trip deviated. POL-RD-01 provides that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree the trace figure governs, and it expressly bars actual_distance_km from the threshold test as a rounded convenience copy. The governing figure is therefore 22.40 km against the booked optimal of 17.6 km, an excess of 4.80 km and 27.3% — clearing both establishment tests, greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km absolute, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00112 is IMPAIRED at weight_multiplier 0.4 on issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and EV-TRIP-00112 carries the same impairment at 0.4.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, whatever the pre-pass tagged. POL-RD-07 bites only on a gap above 90 seconds between fixes, a straight-line jump above 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. EV-GPS-00112 shows gaps [], max_gap_sec 0.0, coverage_pct 100.0 and sample_interval_sec 10.0 against an expected 10.0, so limbs (a) to (c) do not fire and the consequences in POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged. The artifact is IMPAIRED at weight 0.4 with CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, which is a POL-GEN-02 confidence discount only.

The driver cannot shelter behind the stop he says he made, so none of the excess is exonerated as rider-requested. The chat log is COMPLETE at weight 1.0: the rider's MSG-00112-001 carries a platform-resolved waypoint_hint at Paya Lebar Quarter, venue_id VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER, coordinates 1.3175, 103.893, and the driver answered 'ok can' at 18:33:30. POL-RD-04 exonerates a detour only where the trace corroborates the request by passing within 200 m of that waypoint, and the chat artifact's own note records that the trace never comes near it. The exoneration is unavailable and the excess stands. (EV-GPS-00112 is IMPAIRED at 0.4, CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT.)

No external-event exoneration is open to the driver either. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory naming a road, expressway segment or junction that the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the passage. The only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00112-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload, and its absence is itself citable: no LTA advisory covers the PIE or the ECP in the 18:14-18:52 window on 4 August 2026. A driver who wishes to attribute this excess to traffic has nothing to point to.

On POL-RD-08 the rider has carried and shifted the burden. Limb (a) is satisfied — the same trip_id TRP-00112 appears on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown — and limb (b) is satisfied because the excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold and is measured from a trace that, per POL-RD-07, is not impaired under limbs (a) to (c), so the schema-level impairment at weight 0.4 (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT) does not force the measurement onto an independent source. The burden then sits with the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12; his counterparty_statement that he made the stop names no artifact and no clause.

No corroboration overlay applies against this rider. POL-RD-08 raises the bar only where rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer. This rider's deviation_claims_60d is 1, so the overlay is not engaged and the claim is not required to be corroborated beyond the trace.

The money cannot be finally ruled on this record, and POL-RD-10(4) is the trigger. The trip record's started_at is 18:32:10 while the trace's first fix is 18:18:40 — a disagreement of 13 minutes 30 seconds, over the 10-minute limb — and the admissibility report records that this very conflict moves the measured excess across the POL-RD-01 threshold, 27.3% measured over the whole trace against 13.8% measured from started_at. Both artifacts are IMPAIRED at weight 0.4 with CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT. POL-RD-10 is mandatory and terminal: no final ruling issues and the disputed SGD 6.00 is held rather than collected.

POL-RD-10(7) fires on its own terms. The clause's own worked example is a chat_log detour request whose waypoint the gps_trace never approaches, and that is this record exactly: the rider's request with a resolved waypoint_hint and the driver's 'ok can' sit on a COMPLETE, weight-1.0 chat log, the trace never comes near VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER, and the driver's counterparty_statement asserts he did make and wait at that stop. Two sides on admissible and mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength; no final ruling may issue on the money.

Confidence is capped below the platform floor, so escalation is automatic. The deciding fact — the excess measurement — is carried only by EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112, each at weight_multiplier 0.40, and those two are not independent of one another because they are the two sides of the same cross-source conflict. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the cap is therefore the minimum, 0.40, not a maximum over independent carriers. That is below the 0.70 platform-wide floor, so POL-RD-10(1) escalates and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded.

claims.text: The POL-RD-01 threshold is not met on this trip's own trace, and no deviation is established. EV-GPS-00112 begins moving at 18:18:40 and covers 2.38 km before the recorded started_at of 18:32:10 on EV-TRIP-00112 — the admissibility pre-pass measures it — so over the recorded trip window the trace yields 20.02 km against an optimal of 17.6 km. That is an excess of 2.42 km and 13.8 per cent, below POL-RD-01's 20 per cent gate. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH tests to pass (greater than 20 per cent of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km), so the percentage test fails and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. I disclose that EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112 are both IMPAIRED, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight_multiplier 0.4; the pre-pass also records that the trace is otherwise clean — no gap, 100 per cent coverage, 10 second sampling — so within the true trip window its distance is reliable and the only defect is the 13 minute 30 second misalignment with the meter. The rider's threshold showing therefore depends entirely on 2.38 km of movement the trip record says had not begun.

Even on the reading most favourable to the rider — the 22.40 km trace taken at face value and the deviation found established — POL-RD-02 returns the rider nothing. charged_total is 25.26. The recomputed optimal-route fare is ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 17.6 km + 0.28 x 28.0 min) x the surge_multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 optimal-route ERP + 0.00 waiting_time_fee - 0.00 promo_discount = 24.84 + 0.80 = 25.64. Refund = 25.26 - 25.64 = -0.38, floored at zero; a refund below SGD 0.50 is NO_ACTION as de minimis under the same clause. The rider is whole on distance and time on any reading of this record. The charged total and surge come from EV-FARE-00112, complete at weight 1.0; the optimal distance and duration come from EV-TRIP-00112, impaired, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, weight 0.4, which I disclose — and the rider does not dispute the 17.6 km figure, it is her own. There is also no pass-through line to correct under POL-RD-09: erp_gantries on EV-FARE-00112 is an empty array and no toll, surcharge or waiting fee is charged.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established against this driver, so POL-RD-06 changes nothing. POL-RD-06 establishes a pattern only where driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3 or more, or where deviation_flags_90d divided by completed_trips_90d is 0.05 or more with at least 40 completed trips in 90 days. On EV-DPROF-00112, deviation_flags_90d is 1 and completed_trips_90d is 296 — a ratio of 0.0034, an order of magnitude below the gate and nowhere near it. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags also reads 1, but POL-RD-06 names only the trailing-90-day field and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting the lifetime counter for it. There is accordingly no basis to resolve a finely balanced record against the driver under POL-RD-06(a), no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b), and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c).

On the alternative branch where the trace is taken at face value — the branch the driver's own statement supports, the application having shown the trip as not started — it is the driver who is owed money, not the rider. EV-FARE-00112 bills distance_charged_km of 20.00; EV-GPS-00112 records 22.40 km actually driven. The shortfall of 2.40 km exceeds the 1.0 km gate in the final limb of POL-RD-04, and at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre the driver is owed 0.75 x 2.40 = SGD 1.80, already a multiple of SGD 0.05 and well inside the SGD 15.00 cap. The billed figure is not a copy of the trace figure — the pre-pass on EV-FARE-00112 says so expressly — so it is an independent record of what the rider was actually charged, and the shortfall is carried by two independent artifacts, the trace at 0.4 (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, disclosed) and the ledger at 1.0. On that branch the ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both at SGD 1.80, and the rider's charge stands.

If the tribunal will not choose a reading of the cross-source conflict, the case cannot be finally ruled and must escalate — which also leaves the disputed fare unrefunded. POL-RD-10(4) is engaged: the recorded started_at on EV-TRIP-00112 (18:32:10) and the first movement on EV-GPS-00112 (18:18:40) are two admitted timestamps on the same trip disagreeing by 13 minutes 30 seconds, over the 10 minute limb. POL-RD-10(1) is engaged on the same facts through POL-GEN-02(2): the trace and the trip record are the only artifacts carrying the deciding measurement, each at weight_multiplier 0.4, so confidence cannot exceed 0.40 against a floor of 0.70, and both are impaired on issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, which I disclose. Escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal and replaces the ruling, so no money moves and the fare is held rather than refunded. The evidence that would resolve it is a corrected trip start or an independent record of the vehicle's position between 18:18:40 and 18:32:10.

The rider's Paya Lebar Quarter request does not convert into a refund, and it does not exonerate anything either. EV-CHAT-00112 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and shows the rider asking to pass by Paya Lebar Quarter, with waypoint_hint resolved to VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER, and the driver answering 'ok can'. But POL-RD-04 exonerates distance only where the trace corroborates the instruction by passing within 200 m of that waypoint, and the pre-pass records that this trace never comes near it; the clause cannot be run on this record and excludes no excess. Nor does any clause in this category refund a fare for an omitted requested stop: on a METERED trip with quoted_fare_sgd null, the only monetary route open to a rider is the POL-RD-02 recomputation, which returns nil on these figures. The chat log is therefore not a refundable line, and the rider's grievance about the missed stop is not a monetary claim.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute cannot be finally decided on the record before me, so under POL-RD-10 it goes to a human reviewer. The disputed SGD 6.00 is held — neither collected nor refunded — and no compensation is paid today.

What the case turns on. Everything depends on how far the trip actually went, and the two records of that disagree in a way that decides the outcome. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00112 runs 22.40 km and starts moving at 18:18:40. The trip record EV-TRIP-00112 says the trip started at 18:32:10 and the meter billed 20.00 km. The 13-minute-30-second gap means the trace covers 2.38 km before the meter says the trip began. Measured across the whole trace the excess over the 17.6 km optimal is 4.80 km and 27.3%, which clears POL-RD-01's 20% gate and would establish a deviation; measured only from the recorded start it is 2.42 km and 13.8%, which does not. Either the meter started late (and the trace is the trip) or the trace carries the tail of a previous job (and the meter is the trip). Nothing in the bundle decides which, and that one choice flips the finding. This is the POL-RD-10(4) trigger: two admitted artifacts disagree about when the trip began by more than the 10-minute limb.

The confidence floor fails independently. Under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence cannot exceed the weight of the artifacts that carry the deciding measurement. That measurement is carried by EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112, each impaired at weight_multiplier 0.40 with issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT. EV-FARE-00112 (weight 1.0) does not lift the cap: its 20.00 km is the meter's own figure and restates one side of the same conflict, and POL-RD-01 expressly bars that figure from the threshold test. The cap is therefore 0.40 against the 0.70 platform floor, and POL-RD-10(1) escalates automatically. Because the ruling relies on artifacts below weight 1.0, I record them here as POL-GEN-02(3) requires — EV-GPS-00112 and EV-TRIP-00112, each 0.40, issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT — and confirm the finding does not survive the discount: the discount itself is what requires escalation.

What I can settle now, and it does not change the outcome. The trace is impaired at the schema level but clean at the policy level: POL-RD-07's own limbs do not fire — no gap above 90 seconds (max_gap 0.0), no straight-line jump above 500 m, 100% coverage at a 10-second sampling interval — so the trace stays usable and the impairment is only the POL-GEN-02(2) discount, not the corroboration requirement in POL-RD-07(ii) or POL-RD-10(3). No repeat-deviation pattern is established against the driver (deviation_flags_90d 1 against 296 completed trips in 90 days, a ratio of about 0.003), so POL-RD-06 neither breaks a balanced record, nor uplifts the remedy, nor produces a conduct referral; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the field POL-RD-06 names and cannot be substituted for it under POL-GEN-01.

On the Paya Lebar Quarter stop: the chat log EV-CHAT-00112 (weight 1.0) records the rider's request with the platform-resolved waypoint and the driver's 'ok can', and the trace never comes within 200 m of that waypoint, so POL-RD-04 cannot exonerate any part of the route for the driver. ruling.explanation:
To both of you — this case cannot be finally decided on the present record. It goes to a human reviewer, and the SGD 6.00 in dispute is held rather than collected or refunded. No money moves.

Why it escalates. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00112) says the trip began at 18:32:10. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00112) is already moving at 18:18:40 and covers 2.38 km before that. Two admitted artifacts therefore date the start of the same trip 13 minutes 30 seconds apart, over the 10-minute limb in POL-RD-10(4), and that difference decides the case: measured over the whole trace the excess is 4.80 km / 27.3%, over the POL-RD-01 20% gate; measured from the recorded start it is 2.42 km / 13.8%, under the gate. The admissibility pre-pass says expressly that nothing in the bundle decides which reading is correct, and it is right. POL-RD-10(4) is engaged, and POL-RD-10 escalation is terminal.

Confidence independently falls below the floor. The two figures every money outcome rests on — the trace and the trip record — both carry weight_multiplier 0.40 and issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and they are the two sides of one conflict, not independent carriers. POL-GEN-02(2) therefore caps confidence at the minimum, 0.40, against the 0.70 floor, so POL-RD-10(1) fires as well. I have named both impaired artifacts and their issue codes as POL-GEN-02(3) requires.

The limbs, so both of you can see what was and was not decided:

Trace integrity (POL-RD-07, rider's second claim). The pre-pass tagged EV-GPS-00112 IMPAIRED, but for policy purposes the trace is clean: no gaps (max_gap_sec 0.0, gaps empty), 100% coverage, and 10-second sampling against a 10-second expected interval. Limbs (a) to (c) do not fire, so there is no POL-RD-07 impairment and no POL-RD-10(3) consequence. The schema-level impairment is a POL-GEN-02 confidence discount only. Both things are true, and I say both.

Distance and threshold (POL-RD-01, both sides' first claims). Where the trace and the trip record disagree, POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern, so on the trace the deviation is established at 4.80 km and 27.3%; on the trip-window figure it fails at 2.42 km and 13.8%. That disagreement is precisely what escalates, so neither reading is finally adopted.

Refund (POL-RD-02/POL-RD-09, driver's second claim). Taking the trace at face value, charged_total is 25.26 and the recomputed optimal-route fare is 25.64 — ((3.80 + 0.75 x 17.6 + 0.28 x 28.0) x the surge of 1.0 read from the fare breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, waiting fee, promo or surcharge to add or subtract. The refund is therefore nil and would be de minimis NO_ACTION. But that arithmetic itself rests on the impaired trip record's optimal distance and duration, so it cannot be finally ruled either.

Rider-requested stop (POL-RD-04). The chat log (complete, weight 1.0) shows the rider asking for Paya Lebar Quarter with a resolved waypoint and the driver answering 'ok can'. POL-RD-04 exonerates distance only if the trace passes within 200 m of that waypoint, and the trace never comes near it, so the clause exonerates nothing — and no clause in this category turns an omitted requested stop into a refund.

Driver compensation (POL-RD-04 final limb). The driver's alternative branch — ledger 20.00 km against trace 22.40 km, a 2.40 km shortfall, SGD 1.80 — depends on the same unresolved reading of the trace and on the same cross-source conflict; the shortfall is exactly the stretch before the recorded start. It cannot be determined on this record.

Repeat pattern (POL-RD-06). deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 296, a ratio of 0.0034, far below both gates. No pattern, no FULL_REFUND uplift, and no driver-conduct referral. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only and is not the trailing-window field the clause names.

Burden (POL-RD-08). The trip identifiers match across the artifacts and no corroboration overlay applies (deviation_claims_60d is 1), but the excess limb is the very measurement in dispute.

What would resolve it: a corrected trip-start record (or confirmation of whether started_at or the pickup arrival is the pickup event), an independent record of the vehicle's position between 18:18:40 and 18:32:10, or the driver's app-error logs for the evening he mentions. No referral issues from this case: there is no POL-RD-06(c) pattern and no POL-RD-09(4) unmatched charge line (the ERP array is empty and no surcharge is charged).
